name: Civil unrest
summary: French living-cost protests shrink to 82,500 on 21 Nov; general strike in Greece; no deadly nationwide unrest found
state: France's interior ministry counted 82,500 protesters nationwide on 21 Nov, the sixth consecutive Saturday of living-cost protests, against 150,000 claimed by unions (France 24). A strike brought Greece to a standstill, and deadly protests have been reported in Kenya over the building of an Ebola quarantine facility (Morning Star, 26 Nov). Significant protests in several countries keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest or major state crackdown in a large country was found as of 27 Nov.
for_you: Protests and strikes can disrupt transport and public services at short notice. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice for France, Greece and Kenya, which covers demonstrations and strike action.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries — France 82,500 on 21 Nov, Greek strike; no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: France 24 — French interior ministry says 82,500 people protest across country, unions claim 150,000
Morning Star — World in brief: November 26, 2026

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
